statement.purpose: The single statement moment per page: "Nothing needs you." beside the closing pile.

hero.purpose: The home h1, hard left, with the category select inline.

stage.purpose: Stage numerals and titles on the flat page; in the book the title scales with the page.

section.purpose: 24px heads, the wordmark at sm and up.

eyebrow.purpose: Stage strip names, panel labels inside console replicas. Never a kicker over a headline.

label.purpose: Small print: running heads, plate captions, units, field labels.

shadows.name: depth-button
shadows.purpose: Letterpress bottom edge on every solid button and the selected category chip.

shadows.name: depth-panel
shadows.purpose: Sunken panels drawn by inset hairline.

shadows.name: lifted
shadows.purpose: Floating chrome only: nav, stage strip dock, Arby launcher and help panel, menus, the plate's Stop control.

shadows.name: book-shadow
shadows.value: three.js ShadowMaterial, Bottle #0b4030 at 0.2, faded out past the book
shadows.purpose: The only shadow the 3D casts onto the DOM page.

motion.name: curve-overshoot
motion.purpose: Lifts (3px), pops, blooms, the stage dock arriving (260ms; 380ms for the dock).

motion.name: curve-glide
motion.purpose: Slides, fades, develop, the plate sharpening in (160ms), the canvas fading in (420ms), claims opening (320ms).

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Small state changes; stage copy fading between spreads.

motion.name: scroll-crank
motion.value: pure function of scroll: s 0 (shut, hero) to 1-5 (spreads, fractions mid-turn) to 6 (shut on the pile), plus hold within a stage
motion.purpose: Camera, page turns, claim steps and the ribbon lifted by a turning leaf. No state; scrolling back reverses exactly. Every turn takes a camera breath.

motion.name: book-intro
motion.purpose: The hero's shut book arriving; the mini book on scroll into view, leaning to the pointer and riffling on hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Keyframes park on their last frame; the book never starts and the flat page shows.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Plate close-up crop below; two-column claims above.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: Sticky full-window story canvas with copy on the left-hand page above; sticky phone band (max 40svh), 44px touch targets below.

rendering.engine: three.js WebGL2, failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat, frames drawn on demand
rendering.toneMapping: none; sRGB output; palette hexes in, palette hexes out
rendering.light: Hemisphere (#ffffff sky, #e9ece6 ground) at π × 0.4 plus a directional key from (0.62, 0.76, 0.14) at π × 0.6 / key.y, so a flat page takes exactly π and renders #FFFFFF
rendering.shadows: PCF, map 4096 desktop / 2048 phone, radius 7 / 4, frustum follows the book
rendering.depthOfField: BokehPass, desktop only; hero shut book 0.85 (focus mid-cover), closing pile 0.6 (focus the job's book on top); focus is the focus point's view-space depth; aperture 0.0012 × strength, maxblur 0.012 × strength; zero on every resting spread

materials.cloth: MeshPhysical, Bottle, woven height field, roughness 0.86, sheen 0.5 #4f7f68
materials.deboss: MeshPhysical, Bottle ink, alpha and bump from the category pressing, sheen 0.4 #5f8f78
materials.ribbon: MeshPhysical, Sprout satin, roughness 0.3, sheen 1 #e9ffd6; lies on the right-hand page by the gutter; a turning leaf's root lifts and tips it, slipping it toward the fold; once the leaf passes upright it drops back onto the new page over the next 0.9 rad of turn (smoothstep, no bounce); head tucked over the head edge; tail a fixed 2.4 units past the bend over the tail edge, hanging straight down to the table (or down the front of the pile) and lying on it if it reaches; width always in the carrying surface

rendering.geometry: page 16 × 10 (16:10, a console capture), boards 0.16 thick standing 0.22 proud, screen margin 3%
rendering.screens: posters 2048 webp per stage; recordings MP4 1920 desktop / 1280 phone, muted, looped, one at a time, only at rest
rendering.handoff: at rest the HTML plate is laid exactly over the printed screen and fades in over 160ms
rendering.stills: public/book/stills (hero, pile, three plan volumes) rendered from the engine, each with a provenance .json sidecar
rendering.fallback: flat page on reduced motion, no hardware WebGL2, failed start, lost context or a struggling phone; set before first paint via html[data-book]
rendering.leftPage: Bricolage 800 numeral and mono running head and caption by the gutter; no rule under the running head

narrative.overview:
The site is the console's own register (a white page, Panel cells, Bottle for structure, Sprout for the one thing to do next) with one physical object on it: the job, bound as a book in woven Bottle cloth and lit by a window to the right. The white page is the table. The book drops onto it in the hero, opens, and the reader's scroll turns its leaves from enquiry to paid, one spread per stage, each right-hand page holding a real console screen square-on. At the close the book shuts and goes on the season's pile, spines titled with jobs. Everything around the book is the ruled sheet: hairline column rules, registration marks, Bottle and Panel bands, oversized Bricolage set hard left.

The 3D is lit like a product shot, but every flat thing stays its exact hex. The light is calibrated so a page lying face up takes exactly π (hemisphere plus the key's share at its angle), and nothing is tone mapped, so white stock renders #FFFFFF and a printed screen renders exactly as captured. That is why the screen can hand over to a sharp HTML plate whenever the camera rests, with no seam. Shading, soft Bottle-tinted shadows, cloth sheen and depth of field belong to things that are tilted, turning or not being read.

Density is calm and generous: one idea per row, big type with charged empty paper around it, one accent per view. The scroll is a crank: every turn and claim step is a pure function of scroll position, so scrolling back plays everything backwards exactly. Reduced motion, no hardware WebGL2, a lost context or a low-power phone get the flat page, which carries the same screens and engine-rendered stills of the same book.
keyCharacteristics: One register with the console: white and Panel grounds, Bottle structure, one Sprout action.
The book is the site's object; the leaf is its flat DOM page.
Lit 3D, unlit screens: calibrated light, no tone mapping, HTML plate at rest.
Hairline construction: column rules, registration marks, whole-block colour.
Bricolage 800 as interface, hard left; Martian Mono only as small uppercase labels.
Slightly rounded on one scale (6 / 4 / 2px); letterpress depth on content, blur only on floating chrome.

rules.name: The One Sprout Rule
rules.body: One Sprout action per view. The hero and the final band each carry the Sprout trial button; the nav's trial button is Bottle; plan buttons are Bottle. Two Sprout buttons in a view means there is no headline action.

rules.name: The Exact Hex Rule
rules.body: Anything flat stays its hex, in CSS and in the 3D alike. The book's materials are the palette's hexes (palette.ts mirrors globals.css); the canvas is transparent over the page's own white; shadows on the page are Bottle at 0.2 opacity, never grey or black.

rules.name: The Whole Block Rule
rules.body: Colour arrives edge to edge (a Bottle band, a Panel band, a Panel cell). The band redefines the rule and mark inks so the sheet's construction stays continuous across it.

rules.name: The Print-Only Rule
rules.body: Acid and Cream never appear on screen. Arby's crest lime is fixed artwork, not a UI colour.

rules.name: The 800 Only Rule
rules.body: Bricolage is set at 800 with no added letter spacing; the opsz axis does the tightening. No lighter weights, no faux bold.

rules.name: The Small Print Rule
rules.body: Mono is always uppercase, always 9 or 11px, and always small print: a running head, a caption, a unit, a label. It is never body copy and never a line set above a headline to introduce it.

rules.name: The Lit Object, Unlit Screen Rule
rules.body: The book, its cloth, paper, ribbon and arbour are lit, shaded and shadowed. A real console screen is never lit, never tone mapped, never blurred: it sits square-on at real size, and at rest the HTML plate takes over exactly on top of it. No bloom, glow, vignette or glass anywhere.

rules.name: The Calibrated Light Rule
rules.body: A page lying flat takes exactly π of light. Change the light, the materials or the camera and the flat page must still render #FFFFFF, or the plate handoff shows a seam.

rules.name: The Depth of Field Rule
rules.body: Bokeh runs on desktop only, and only on shots where no screen is being read: the hero's shut book (strength 0.85, focused mid-cover) and the closing pile (0.6, focused on the job's book on top). Focus is the focus point's view-space depth, never its straight-line distance; aperture is 0.0012 × strength and maxblur 0.012 × strength. Strength is zero on every resting spread.

rules.name: The Paper Lifts Rule
rules.body: In the DOM, a pointed-at leaf or button lifts 3px toward the reader on the overshoot curve. A state is a position, never a colour wash.

dos: Do keep every flat surface its exact hex, in CSS and in three.js; the canvas stays transparent over the page's own white.
Do light the book with the calibrated rig (a flat page takes exactly π) and keep tone mapping off, so white stock is #FFFFFF and screens read as captured.
Do hand a resting screen to the HTML plate, square-on and at real size; only the moves between rests are 3D.
Do drive every camera move, page turn and claim step from scroll position alone, so it reverses exactly.
Do use the book's own verbs for state: shut, opened, turned, shelved. In the DOM, lift 3px.
Do keep one Sprout action per view; the nav's trial button stays Bottle.
Do set Bricolage 800 hard left with charged empty paper around it, and print numbers in Bricolage.
Do give the flat page the same screens, and engine-rendered stills of the same book, each raster with a provenance sidecar.
Do keep depth of field to the hero and the pile, desktop only.
Do keep touch targets at 44px below 1024px.
donts: Don't light, shade, tone map, blur or reflect a console screen.
Don't add bloom, glow, vignette, glass or a CSS gradient. Light falling across the book is not a gradient; a CSS gradient is.
Don't tilt a dashboard or float UI in space; screens live on the page.
Don't let a hairline, rule or mark cross a page or a screen inside the story.
Don't wash a leaf, a book or a stage with colour to show state.
Don't put Acid or Cream on screen, or recolour Arby or the wordmark.
Don't round above 6px or cast a blurred shadow from content; blur belongs to floating chrome.
Don't set mono as body copy, or as a kicker line above a headline.
Don't show a resting screen with depth of field, or a screen that scrolls inside its frame.
